title: Admin Orchestrator: Playlet Compiler and Diagnostic Helpers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight 'playlet' compiler that converts authored runbook steps (Markdown + typed inputs) into idempotent, parameterized tasklets that can be executed by the Ops Runner. Include a small diagnostics helper library for safe dry-run validation, permission checks, and preflight telemetry hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Authoring: Confluence/Markdown runbook with typed inputs is parsed and yields a validated playlet JSON manifest
Execution: Ops Runner can execute a compiled playlet step-by-step with rollback hooks configured
Safety: Playlet compiler enforces idempotency annotations and denies unsafe shell actions by default
Observability: Each playlet execution emits structured telemetry to the Admin Telemetry dashboard with latency, success/failure, and tokenized costing estimates
Integrations: CLI and Console UI surface compiled playlets for manual invocation and scheduled runs
tasks: Design manifest schema and idempotency annotations (2 days)
Prototype parser for Markdown runbook -> playlet manifest (3 days)
Implement dry-run validator with permission checks (2 days)
Hook telemetry events into existing Admin Telemetry pipeline (3 days)
Add safe-exec shim and rollback pattern to Ops Runner (4 days)
Console listing endpoint and basic UI surfaces for playlets (3 days)
Integration tests and a sample migration playlet with end-to-end smoke test (3 days)
risks: Over-permissive playlets could enable accidental data changes if idempotency is not enforced
Telemetry cardinality may spike if we emit per-step events without sampling
Auth model mismatch between Console and Ops Runner could cause execution failures
Edge cases in converting free-text runbook steps to typed inputs could require manual authoring conventions
mitigations: Default compiled playlets to 'dry-run' mode until an explicit allowlist is applied
Emit coarse-grained telemetry by default and provide opt-in detailed traces
Use a simple capability token model for playlet execution scoped to specific actions
Ship authoring guidelines and a linting tool to surface ambiguous steps at compile time
metrics: Number of playlets authored and executed per week
Mean time to execute a playlet (ms)
Percentage of playlet runs that used dry-run vs live execution
Reduction in manual steps per incident (target 40% within quarter)
Telemetry event volume and dropped-sample rate
comments: 2026-03-05: Kickoff sync with SRE and Oncall docs team. Agreed to keep authoring format Markdown-first with a lightweight frontmatter for typed inputs.
2026-03-06: Design review - UX wants an additional human-readable summary field included in the manifest for Console hovercards.
2026-03-08: Miguel implemented initial parser prototype. Parser handles bullets and fenced code blocks but needs better handling for conditional steps.
2026-03-10: Security review requested; SecOps suggested capability tokens and an allowlist for 'mutating' primitives.
2026-03-12: Dry-run validator integrated with Admin Telemetry; added sampling to prevent event surge during early trials. Planning staging rollout to internal SRE team next week.
notes: We intentionally call the unit 'playlet' to distinguish small, composable runbook fragments from larger playbooks. Aim to keep compiled manifests small (< 4KB) and human-auditable.
deployment_plan: Stage 0: Internal dev preview - local CLI + dry-run only
Stage 1: Staging cluster - enable live exec for whitelisted playlets
Stage 2: Canary - small SRE cohort in prod with monitoring alarms
Stage 3: Full GA - Console listing and self-serve authoring
